subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In incomplete dominance, a cross between a red (RR) and white (rr) flower gives pink offspring. The F2 phenotypic ratio from crossing two pink plants is:
questions.explain: With incomplete dominance the heterozygote is pink, so the F2 shows a 1:2:1 genotype-matched phenotype ratio.

questions.q: Restriction endonucleases that leave 'sticky ends' are useful in recombinant DNA technology because:
options: They cut DNA into blunt fragments only
The single-stranded overhangs allow complementary fragments to anneal before ligation
They permanently join DNA without ligase
questions.explain: Sticky ends are short single-stranded overhangs that base-pair with complementary ends, allowing DNA ligase to join the fragments.

options: A small group establishes a new population carrying only a subset of the original gene pool
A large population is split equally by a barrier
questions.explain: A few founding individuals carry only part of the parent population's genetic variation, skewing allele frequencies in the new population.

questions.q: A tRNA anticodon is 5'-UAC-3'. The mRNA codon it pairs with is:
questions.explain: Antiparallel complementary base pairing of anticodon 5'-UAC-3' gives codon 5'-GUA-3'.

questions.q: A transmission electron microscope (TEM) differs from a scanning electron microscope (SEM) in that the TEM:
options: passes electrons through a thin specimen to give a high-resolution 2D image of internal structure
has lower resolution than the SEM
can be used on living specimens
questions.explain: A TEM transmits electrons through an ultra-thin section, producing a detailed 2D image of internal ultrastructure, whereas an SEM gives a 3D surface view.

questions.q: In PCR, the temperature is raised to around 95 degrees C in order to:
options: Separate the two DNA strands by breaking hydrogen bonds
questions.explain: Denaturation at ~95 degrees C breaks the hydrogen bonds, separating the DNA into single strands.

options: Both alleles' phenotypes fully and simultaneously
questions.explain: In codominance both alleles are expressed fully in the heterozygote, as in the AB blood group.

questions.q: The ABO blood group system is an example of multiple alleles because:
options: There are more than two alleles in the population for one gene
Each person has more than two alleles
questions.explain: Three alleles (IA, IB, i) exist in the population for the single ABO gene, though each individual carries only two.

questions.q: Chloroplasts are adapted for photosynthesis by containing:
options: thylakoid membranes stacked into grana bearing chlorophyll, surrounded by stroma
questions.explain: Grana (stacks of thylakoids) hold chlorophyll for the light-dependent reactions, while the stroma is the site of the light-independent reactions.

questions.q: Increased methylation of DNA in a gene's promoter region typically results in:
options: A change in the DNA base sequence
questions.explain: Promoter methylation usually prevents transcription factor binding, inhibiting transcription without altering the base sequence.

questions.q: The genetic code is described as 'degenerate'. This means that:
options: Some codons do not code for any amino acid
Each codon codes for more than one amino acid
Most amino acids can be coded for by more than one codon
questions.explain: Degeneracy means most amino acids are specified by more than one triplet codon.

questions.q: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to the 3' end of a strand. This explains why:
options: Helicase is required to join the fragments
The lagging strand is synthesised discontinuously as Okazaki fragments
The leading strand is synthesised in fragments
questions.explain: Because synthesis must run 5' to 3', the antiparallel lagging strand is built discontinuously as Okazaki fragments later joined by ligase.
